decision: Use a thin per-call qrexec campaign harness that signs the existing worker envelope, invokes qrexec-client-vm once per request, emits raw JSONL evidence, and leaves aggregation/readiness decisions to the existing collector and gate.
selected: process-per-call qrexec transport plus declarative fault/probe steps

criteria.correctness: Reuses the production signed-envelope and coordinator response contracts; crash-retry explicitly uses the same requestId across fault and recovery services.
criteria.robustness: Fails closed on malformed coordinator replies, unexpected fault-service success, unsupported step modes, missing target/service, or transport non-zero exit.
criteria.latency: Measures the actual qrexec round trip at the process boundary and records recovery latency separately.
criteria.resourceUse: No daemon, database, telemetry backend, or persistent harness state; one qrexec process per request mirrors the intended Qubes service lifecycle.
criteria.regressionRisk: Adds an adapter and tests without changing mission queue, durable journal, authentication, or coordinator semantics.
criteria.qa: Unit tests cover clean evidence, crash/retry service switching, stale-completion detection, QA-before-join detection, and fail-closed fault injection.

alternatives.name: Qubes-specific orchestration logic inside the coordinator
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Would duplicate transport concerns inside durable mission semantics and increase regression surface.

alternatives.name: Long-lived network or qrexec daemon
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Adds lifecycle, listening-surface, memory, and recovery complexity before process-per-call VM-boundary behavior is proven.

alternatives.name: Manual shell campaign and hand-authored summary counters
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Not replayable in CI and can hide evidence-generation mistakes or omit failures.

lessons: Fault injection must use a dedicated fault service and a normal recovery service; a permanently configured crash hook would crash every retry.
Readiness evidence should be derived from raw responses and transport failures rather than trusted precomputed counters.
The Qubes harness should remain transport-only so the same mission and reconciliation semantics are exercised across process and VM boundaries.
safety: Synthetic defensive workloads only. No real payment credentials, financial transactions, fraud workflows, or security-control weakening.
